title: Environmental Movement Practice
subtitle: Individualized movement education built around real environments, physical capacity, technical skill, and creative exploration.
system: Environmental Movement Practice is a phase-based movement education system built around real environments, not controlled gym conditions alone.

We design individualized phases of work using the terrain, tools, and movement opportunities available to the student. A phase may include parkour tasks, jumping and landing drills, acrobatic work, strength and physical preparation, rolling, climbing, and more open creative exploration.

The student receives written prescriptions and demonstration videos, practices the material independently, and sends back footage of key drills, lines, and benchmarks. We review the footage, give precise feedback, adjust the constraints, and build the next step of the process.
This makes the practice structured without becoming rigid, and exploratory without becoming random.

steps.title: Assess the terrain and the mover
steps.description: We look at what the student has available: rocks, logs, walls, bars, branches, slopes, open space, and the current capacities and interests they bring to the work.

steps.title: Build a phase of practice
steps.description: Each phase organizes the work into clear categories: technical drills, environmental tasks, strength work, movement lines, and exploratory practice.

steps.title: Practice independently
steps.description: You train independently in your real environment.

steps.title: Film key pieces
steps.description: Film drills, benchmarks, and movement lines — the most revealing parts of the work.

steps.title: Review and refine
steps.description: We review the footage and respond with cues, corrections, demonstrations, and sometimes entirely new constraints that sharpen the task.

steps.title: Progress and repeat
steps.description: The work evolves through clearer movement, stronger positions, softer landings, better coordination, more environmental confidence, and milestone completion. Each round becomes the basis for the next phase.

groups.title: Environmental Parkour
groups.description: Route finding, stepping patterns, environmental lines, obstacle negotiation, and the ability to move through built and natural spaces with clarity and adaptability.

groups.title: Jumping & Landing
groups.description: Jump phases, precision jumps, landing mechanics, elastic rebounding, arm timing, trajectory control, and the ability to express force cleanly.

groups.title: Acrobatics & Inversion
groups.description: Wall-supported handstands, kickups, cartwheel catches, inversion shapes, shoulder organization, and free association through acrobatic patterns.

groups.title: Physical Preparation / Strength
groups.description: Whole-body strength work that supports skill expression: split squats, pushup variations, elastic strength tasks, loaded work, and later pulling and mantling capacity.

groups.title: Rolling & Ground Contact
groups.description: Forward rolls, contact organization, absorbing force through the body, and learning how the ground can become part of fluent movement rather than an interruption.

groups.title: Climbing / Pulling / Traversal
groups.description: Using bars, rings, branches, rocks, and ledges to build pulling strength, climb onto the environment, mantle, descend with control, and expand what routes become possible.

groups.title: Creative Integration
groups.description: Free association, rhythm work, dynamic variation, movement lines, and the ability to synthesize techniques into living movement rather than isolated drills.

formats.title: Drills
formats.description: Focused technical work used to sharpen one pattern or one quality at a time.

formats.title: Strength Sets
formats.description: Physical preparation that builds the capacity to express movement more powerfully and more reliably.

formats.title: Benchmarks
formats.description: Clear repeatable tasks that let us measure progress without reducing the whole practice to numbers.

formats.title: Lines
formats.description: Short sequences through the environment that connect multiple skills into a coherent route.

formats.title: Free Association
formats.description: Open rounds where the student integrates material more creatively and reveals what is becoming natural.

formats.title: Environmental Tasks
formats.description: Movement problems shaped by the terrain itself: a wall, a curb, a rock, a ledge, a branch, or a line through space.

milestone_intro: Progress in this system is not abstract. Each phase can include simple milestones that make development visible.

milestones.title: Kickups
milestones.criterion: consecutive successful holds in each shape

milestones.title: Cartwheel catches
milestones.criterion: consecutive successful holds in each shape

milestones.title: Acrobatic free association
milestones.criterion: 60–90 seconds with skills shown clearly on both sides

difference: This is not generic fitness programming, and it is not a static video library.

The work is built around the student’s actual environment, actual practice, and actual movement questions. It combines technical precision with creative exploration. It treats strength, skill, coordination, perception, and adaptability as connected. And it evolves through direct feedback rather than staying frozen as a one-size-fits-all plan.

cta.heading: Interested in This Kind of Practice?
cta.body: Environmental Movement Practice is for people who want a deeper, more individualized relationship to movement — one that develops real capacity, real skill, and real adaptability in the environments they actually inhabit.
